mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive or not significantly different from baseline during periods when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive monthly INDPRO declines exceeding -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.3% month-over-month indicates a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with disinflation, which historically has been associated with higher equity volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by more than -0.3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between housing starts (HOUST) and personal income (PAYEMS) over the past six months signals robust household balance sheets and future consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Pearson correlation(HOUST, PAYEMS) > 0.7 over last 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when the correlation between HOUST and PAYEMS exceeds 0.7 over the prior six months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during periods when PAYEMS grows by more than 0.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) over three consecutive months, coupled with flat or declining consumption (GDPC1), indicates households are accumulating cash rather than spending, which historically precedes a delayed but pronounced consumption rebound and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 is flat or declining
regime_hint: household savings accumulation with flat consumption
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS rises for three consecutive months and GDPC1 is flat or declining.
